messages:
acme_app_eng: Hey team, ran into a weird quota behavior during a prolonged streaming job. UI showed credits restored ~5m after depletion but the API continued returning 429s for ~25m. Tenant: acme-42, request_id: r-8c9f2aa
sara_support: Sorry about that. Can you paste the exact UTC window and any 429 headers you observed (X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset)?
acme_app_eng: Window 2024-06-02T03:12:10Z -> 2024-06-02T03:40:00Z. Logs show 429s with `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 1717353600`. UI showed +12 credits around 03:17 but API stayed 429 until ~03:42.
leon_infra: Two quick hypotheses: (1) stream token accounting: tokens are debited as theyre emitted server-side vs acked by client, so inflight can consume fast. (2) there's a short-lived quota replica cache that can allow the UI to display a refreshed balance before the frontends have their caches invalidated.
acme_app_eng: How long is that cache typically? 25 minutes sounds long for a cache mismatch.
maya_product: Cache is usually on the order of seconds->a few minutes. 25m suggests either a delayed top-up job/ledger write or a routing split where some frontends never received the invalidate signal.
leon_infra: Can you grep for ledger/topup events around the refill? Look for `billing.topup.success tenant=acme-42` and frontend `quota-cache-invalidate tenant=acme-42`.
acme_app_eng: Found ledger: `billing.topup.success tenant=acme-42 amount=1200 ts=2024-06-02T03:16:55Z id=topup-77`. Frontend shows `WARN quota-cache-miss tenant=acme-42 ts=2024-06-02T03:20:10Z` but no explicit invalidate line immediately after topup.
quota_bot: system: Observed an in-flight retry storm for tenant acme-42 between 2024-06-02T03:12:00Z and 2024-06-02T03:22:00Z (~82 retries). Recommend customers back off; retries consumed newly topped credits as soon as they arrived.
sara_support: Practical repro steps for the customer: (1) run a controlled stream that logs server token counts and request_ids. (2) on receiving 429s, pause retries for 10-20s and re-try single request. If it succeeds after pause, likely retry-storm. (3) provide `billing.topup.success` id and sample request_ids to infra if issue persists.
acme_app_eng: Good plan. To confirm: the X-RateLimit-Reset header we saw (1717353600) is unix secs for ~03:20Z? That seemed mismatched with the UI refill time.
leon_infra: The reset header is the ledger's next reset epoch; can be influenced by regional clocks. Also if frontends are still draining retries you'll get 429s until the retry pressure subsides even if `Remaining` > 0 briefly.
acme_app_eng: Anything infra can do to reduce customer impact in the short term?
leon_infra: Server-side mitigations: (a) publish immediate cache invalidates on topup (we're rolling a fix today), (b) return `Retry-After` on aggressive retryers to discourage tight loops, (c) rate-limit per-client-IP on spikes so one client doesn't burn the tenant bucket.
maya_product: Also update docs/SDK: recommend exponential backoff with jitter and to check `X-RateLimit-Reset` before heavy retry. We'll add a note in the streaming best-practices doc.
sara_support: I'll attach `topup-77` to the customer ticket and ask acme to paste request ids once they run repro.
acme_app_eng: Thanks all. I'll run the repro against a staging tenant with controlled retries and post logs + request ids in follow-up.
leon_infra: Noted. We'll monitor `topup-77` and watch for similar patterns across tenants. If we see correlated retry storms, we can temporarily throttle aggressive clients at the edge and follow up with the customer.
